trust_decision.summary: Credential headers X-Kerberos-Hub-PublicKey/X-Kerberos-Hub-PrivateKey must not survive a redirect to a different host; net/http only strips its own standard sensitive headers, so the project must supply CheckRedirect on the client it builds.

landing_point.why: The summary names 'redirect-following HTTP client without CheckRedirect'; this is the only client construction named by the upload path, where the Hub headers are set four lines above and client.Do follows redirects by default.

fix_sites.module_kind: internal worker function, TLS-insecure client branch

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The two verify handlers are settings/test endpoints, not the recording upload flow the advisory describes, so a solver can call them diagnostics that never carry real footage.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Redirects must still be followed for the upload: HubURI is operator-supplied and a hub deployment can legitimately answer /storage/upload with a same-host or regional-host redirect, so a fix that returns http.ErrUseLastResponse (or strips the headers unconditionally) breaks successful uploads; the credentials only need to go when the host actually changes.

O6_input_shapes: two request methods through one client: HEAD preflight and POST body upload
both client branches: AGENT_TLS_INSECURE=true transport and default client

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /api/hub/verify -> cloud.VerifyHub sends X-Kerberos-Hub-PublicKey and X-Kerberos-Hub-PrivateKey (taken straight from the request body) through a default/InsecureSkipVerify http.Client with no CheckRedirect
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a connectivity check against /subscription/verify, a neighbouring feature to the storage upload, so it reads as 'verify' rather than as a credential-carrying upload.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, separate file Cloud.go; 1 route registration and 1 file from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /api/persistence/verify with cloud=kerberoshub/s3 -> cloud.VerifyPersistence POSTs test-480p.mp4 to HubURI/storage/upload with the same two Hub headers via a default client with no CheckRedirect
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It only uploads the bundled sample file during settings verification, so a solver can argue it is a test path outside the advisory's real-upload flow.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, separate file Cloud.go; ~970 lines after the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A Vault-upload client built with the same three-line if/else and no CheckRedirect, sending X-Kerberos-Storage-CloudKey/AccessKey/SecretAccessKey.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the exact copy-paste pattern used in five places in the cloud package; a maintainer adding a hub-proxied upload or a shared credential header would land here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Heartbeat POST to HubURI that already ships cloudpublickey in the body could be extended with an X-Kerberos-Hub-* auth header on the same shared client.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The heartbeat already authenticates to the Hub and already owns a long-lived http.Client built at Cloud.go:223-231, so adding a header there needs no new plumbing.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A Vault verify upload inside VerifyPersistence that mirrors the Hub verify block header-for-header.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The Hub and Vault branches of VerifyPersistence are near-duplicates; a new provider branch is normally written by copying one of them.

O9_family: sensitive data exposure / credential leakage to an attacker-controlled redirect target (CWE-200, CWE-522); missing redirect policy on an outbound HTTP client
